questions.q: What does ServiceNow's data archiving and rotation capability actually do?
options: Permanently and immediately deletes any record older than 30 days with no option to retain it
Moves records matching defined criteria out of the live, active table into an archive table, or deletes per a defined retention rule
Automatically compresses every table on the instance regardless of record age
Prevents any new records from being created on a table
questions.explain: Archiving moves old, rarely-accessed records out of the active table based on defined criteria — it doesn't discard history by default.

questions.q: How does archiving connect to course 12's indexing and query-performance content, per this lesson?
options: It doesn't connect at all — archiving and indexing solve unrelated problems
A smaller active table is faster to query and index, so archiving and good indexing both serve the same performance goal from different angles
Archiving replaces the need for any indexing on a table
Indexing only matters on archive tables, not active ones
questions.explain: Archiving shrinks the active table's working set, which is faster to query and index regardless of indexing quality — the same performance goal as course 12's indexing content, approached differently.

questions.q: What is the real tradeoff an architect must balance when designing a retention/archiving policy?
options: There is no real tradeoff — archiving is always a pure performance win with no downside
Query performance on the active table versus the business or compliance need to keep historical data readily accessible
Disk cost versus CPU cost only
Whether the instance should be single-instance or multi-instance
questions.explain: Archived data becomes less immediately accessible to end users and reports, so performance gains have to be weighed against real accessibility needs like audits or legal holds.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a 3-year retention window can't be treated as a universal default across every table?
options: Because 3 years is always too short for every table on every platform
Because the right window depends on what that specific business actually does with its old data, and has to be confirmed against real compliance requirements
Because ServiceNow technically enforces a fixed 3-year window platform-wide
Because archiving criteria cannot be customized per table
questions.explain: A sound policy is a judgment call made with the business, grounded in actual usage and compliance needs — not a one-size-fits-all technical setting.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why does conflating "archive to a separate table" with "delete outright" count as a real risk?
options: Because they are functionally identical outcomes with no difference
Because they are very different outcomes — one keeps the data queryable in an archive table, the other removes it entirely — and a policy should decide between them deliberately
Because ServiceNow doesn't support archiving to a separate table
Because deletion is always required by compliance regardless of policy
questions.explain: Archiving preserves the data in a separate, queryable table; deletion removes it. A sound policy makes that choice on purpose, not by default.
